newsitem.title: USA: Whole Foods to acquire Amrion.
newsitem.headline: Whole Foods to acquire Amrion.

text.p: Whole Foods Market Inc, the owner of a chain of natural food supermarkets, said late Monday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Amrion Inc for about $146 million.
Under the deal, each share of Amrion is to be exchanged for 0.87 shares of Whole Foods stock, or about 4.6 million Whole Foods shares in total, the company said.
Whole Foods said it expects to take a charge of between $3 million and $5 million for merger-related costs in the fourth quarter ending September 28, 1997.

Whole Foods Chairman and Chief Executive John Mackey said in a statement that the acquisition, excluding those charges, was expected to be non-dilutive toward its 1997 earnings and accretive to its 1998 fiscal year earnings per share.
The transaction has been approved by the board of directors of each company. It must also be approved by shareholders of both companies. The deal is expected to close in September.
Amrion, based in Boulder, Colo., is a producer and marketer of nutritional products, including nutritional supplements, and has about 5.3 million shares outstanding.
Whole Foods said that Amrion Chairman and Chief Executive Mark Crossen will remain as chief executive and will join the Whole Foods executive team and board of directors.
Whole Foods owns and operates a chain of natural food supermarkets.
